_comment: Guild Wares (1.6.0): a gear piece bought at the counter and enchanted on the spot. Forms are 'Plugin|0xID' (no editor IDs: the DLL reads this file as it is).
_kinds: What the gear piece is. list: a vanilla leveled list rolled at the player's level (gear other mods add to it comes along). weight: how often this kind is picked. A rolled item that is already enchanted is rolled again.
_families: The enchantments a ware can carry: vanilla's base enchantments, the ones the enchanting table teaches. Armor ones say themselves which slots they fit (their worn restrictions, as at the table); weapon ones fit any weapon. Their strength comes from vanilla's own tiers of the same enchantment (e.g. Fortify Health 20..70), read at run time.
_tiers: Index 0..3 = Guild, Blessed, Cursed, Heroic. rank: the guild rank that unlocks it (0..5 = E..S; -1 = not offered yet: Heroic waits for Hero status). strength: where in vanilla's tiers of the enchantment it sits, 0 = the weakest vanilla tier, 1 = the strongest. multiplier: the result is then multiplied (Cursed: twice the strongest vanilla item). effects: how many different enchantments (Heroic: two). curse: a Cursed Item also carries one of 'curses'. charge: a weapon's enchantment charge (a grand soul gem fills 3000). name: the tier's English name, which leads the item's new name ('Cursed Steel Mace'; translators: $AG_WareTier_<id>). merit / reputation / gold: the price, all three at once. Reputation is SPENT here, the one place it is: the Guild sells what is in its vaults, but it frowns on members who buy their way to power (the author's lore: a gambler's shortcut).
_sounds: The strongbox's sounds (the counter's notice of a ware bought): the game's own sound records, 'Plugin|0xID'. rattle plays twice as the box shakes, unlock as the lock gives, open as the lid bursts off, and each tier's revealSound as its card rises. Empty = silent. None of them plays when MCM > Audio > Notification sounds is None.
_resistCap: No resistance a ware gives goes past this (percent): a Cursed Item's doubled Resist Poison would otherwise read 200.
_curses: What a Cursed Item costs its owner while it is worn or held: vanilla effects only, and never one that touches Health or max Health (Battle Summaries counts a fall in Health that no blow explains as a wound). On worn items the curse is part of the enchantment, the way vanilla's Necromancer Amulet carries its slower regeneration. Weapons cannot carry it that way (a weapon's enchantment strikes the target), so a cursed weapon's owner gets the curse as an ability while the weapon is equipped: tools/EspGen builds one per entry, 0xFE0 onwards, in this order (append only). note: how the curse reads in the item's description, after 'But ' (<mag> is the magnitude): 'Absorb 80 points of magicka. But you take 50% more damage from shock.' A weapon's description cannot show its owner's curse, and four of these vanilla effects have no text at all, so EspGen also builds two effects per curse that do nothing but carry this note (0xFF0 + 2n for weapons, 0xFF1 + 2n for worn items); the worn one is only added when the vanilla effect has no text of its own.

curses.note: you take <mag>% more damage from fire
